text:
maria: heads-up — CI perf run for canary in euw1 showed a big p99 spike on A10/L4 after merge 1a2b3c4. Blocking rollout.
maria: deploy-bot posted the failed job: https://ci/redwood/jobs/1347 :exclamation:
deploy-bot: [CI] canary-euw1-a10-l4 — p50 45ms -> 48ms, p95 120ms -> 230ms, p99 1100ms -> 4200ms. See artifacts: /artifacts/ci/1347/profile.tar.gz
kevin: :eyes: that's huge. Did the merge touch kernel selection or batching heuristics?
maria: yes — PR #5123 updated kernel-selector to prefer the 'sparse-attn' path for seq_len>256 to help H100, and adjusted continuous-batcher to favor slightly larger batches (target 16 -> 24) when throughput estimate high.
eli: on A10/L4 that selector ends up picking a slow fallback kernel we never stress-tested for medium batch sizes. Also noticed increased KV cache eviction churn in the same window.
kevin: I pulled the profile. The flamegraph shows long waits in netdev_xmit and skb_enqueue around the NIC queue. Lots of TX backpressure at the NIC ring on L4.
maria: snippet from the profile (top lines):
```
  p99 4200ms  token_loop()
    waiting on kv_cache_lock
    netdev_xmit -> skb_queue_tail
    kernel_fallback_sparse_attn()
```
eli: that matches our traces — many requests get routed to the same worker because of the new batcher heuristics, creating a thundering-herd at the TX queue. On A10 the kernel path is more tolerant; on L4 the kernel fallback plus larger batches blow out latency.
kevin: sounds like two interacting changes: kernel-selector and batcher tuning. Which one is higher risk to revert quickly?
maria: revert is faster: `git revert 1a2b3c4` and trigger canary rollback. But we can also hotfix selector to force legacy kernel for A10/L4: set `kselector.override=legacy_for_a10_l4` in config and restart runtime-svc.
runtime-oncall-bot: @maria acknowledged. Rolling action: create rollback MR and pause euw1 canary in rollout service.
eli: ops: for immediate mitigation I'd prefer config override to avoid full rollback. Revert if config patch doesn't reduce p99 under 600ms.
kevin: agreed. Maria can you run the override and post quick perf samples?
maria: applying override now, restarting runtime-svc in euw1-a10-l4 (sudo /infra/bin/restart runtime-svc --region euw1 --nodepool a10-l4). Will post results in ~5m.
maria: quick perf after override (5m): p99 down to 520ms, p95 210ms. Still above baseline but much better. KV cache eviction rate reduced ~3x in metrics.
eli: good. That suggests the selector was main culprit. Still want to revert merge until we have a spec that handles L4 kernel differences.
kevin: create PR to revert + add integration test that runs medium-batch path on an L4-like profile. Tag me.
maria: opened revert PR #5130 (git revert 1a2b3c4 + test), and added `kselector.integration/l4-medium-batch` test. Linking: https://git/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/5130
deploy-bot: [CI] PR #5130 — presubmit started.
eli: other note — networking team saw small burst of packet drops on the nodegroup coincident with the spike. Filing a ticket for NIC driver tuning but not blocking for this rollout revert.
kevin: thanks. Action items:
- maria: keep config override until #5130 merged and canary re-tested (ETA 2-4h)
- eli: add L4-oriented perf test to CI matrix
- runtime-oncall-bot: monitor euw1 a10-l4 p99 and alert if >700ms for 10m
maria: ack. I'll keep posting updates. :thumbsup:
